name: Tax returns
why: A return is the easiest proof of income for a loan, a benefit or an estate. Keep a copy of every one.

name: Receipts and statements behind a return
why: Covers the usual three-year review window and the longer windows for some errors.

name: Pay stubs
why: Check them against the W-2 in January, then shred.

name: Retirement account statements
why: Keep year-end statements and records of after-tax contributions for as long as the account exists.

name: Home purchase and improvement records
why: Improvements raise your cost basis and lower the gain when you sell.

name: Investment purchase records
why: Needed to work out the gain or loss when you sell.

name: Business formation documents
why: Articles, operating agreements, EIN letters and S election approvals.

name: Invoices, receipts and bank statements
why: Support every line of the business return.

name: Fixed asset records
why: Support depreciation for as long as the asset is on the books, and the sale afterwards.

name: Payroll records and W-4s
why: Employment tax records after the tax is due or paid, whichever is later.

name: Contractor W-9s and 1099s
why: Show why you did or did not withhold.

name: Board minutes and grant agreements
why: Nonprofits: governance records and restricted gift terms.
